L9@P1: Definition
L10@P1: A partially ordered set, or poset, is a set P following the properties:
L11@P1: 1 Certain elements x, y ∈ P are relatable under the binary
L12@P1: relation ≤.
L13@P1: 2 If x ≤ y and y ≤ x then x = y.
L14@P1: 3 If x ≤ y, and y ≤ z, then x ≤ z.
L15@P1: Definition
L16@P1: In a poset P, an element y covers an element x if x ≤ y, and there
L17@P1: doesn’t exist a distinct element z such that x ≤ z ≤ y. We write
L18@P1: x l y.

L50@P4: Definition (Stanley)
L51@P4: An r-differential poset P is a poset satisfying the following:
L52@P4: 1 P is locally finite, graded, and has a unique minimal element
L53@P4: Ob.
L54@P4: 2 For every two elements x, y ∈ P, the number of elements
L55@P4: covering both x and y is the same as the number of elements
L56@P4: covered by both x and y.
L57@P4: 3 If an element x ∈ P covers d elements, then r + d elements
L58@P4: cover x.

L161@P13: r-Fibonacci Numbers
L162@P13: Definition
L163@P13: The r-Fibonacci numbers Fr(x) satisfy Fr(0) = 1, Fr(1) = r, and
L164@P13: Fr(x) = r · Fr(x − 1) + Fr(x − 2).
L165@P13: Note that if r = 1, we just get the regular Fibonacci numbers.
L166@P13: Since the reflection-extension construction of the r-Fibonacci poset
L167@P13: consists of reflecting the second to last row, and extending r
L168@P13: elements per element in the last row, the rank sizes of the
L169@P13: r-Fibonacci poset are indeed the r-Fibonacci numbers.
L170@P13: Benjamin Wright

L186@P15: Now, we move on to new results:
L187@P15: Theorem
L188@P15: In a differential poset P, if pn = Fr(n) for some particular n, then
L189@P15: the partial r-differential poset P[0,n]is isomorphic to the
L190@P15: r-Fibonacci poset Z(r)[0,n].
